article.story: DALLAS -- — Kevin Jennings threw three touchdowns to break SMU's career record, Kendrick Raphael ran for 104 yards against his former team while accounting for three scores and the No. 23 Mustangs beat California 59-20 after trailing at halftime on Saturday. The Mustangs (6-1, 4-1 ACC) scored touchdowns on their first six drives after the break. The second of those scores was Jennings' record-breaking 73rd career TD pass, a 21-yarder to Derek McFall, and the third-year starting quarterback added to that with a 17-yarder to Jalen Hale with 6:29 left. “Just all the great quarterbacks that came through here and being able to surpass them, it’s an amazing feeling,” Jennings said. Jennings, 25-8 as the starter and already SMU's career leader for passing yards (9,766) and completions (781), surpassed the 72 TD passes by Tanner Mordecai from 2021-22. Jennings had tied that mark with his 22-yard fourth-down pass to Raphael in the first quarter and finished 16 of 23 passing for 223 yards. “Deservedly so,” Mustangs coach Rhett Lashlee said. “He just continues to do what he does best, which is win.” Freshman running back Christian Rhodes had TD runs of 5 and 3 yards in SMU's scoring surge in the second half, which Cal (3-5, 2-3) opened with three consecutive three-and-outs. Raphael, who played for the Bears last season, had another fourth-down touchdown with a 1-yard run that tied the game at 17-17 with 1:57 left before halftime. Towns McGough then made a half-ending field goal to put Cal up 20-17. “We can’t just win one half,” Cal coach Tosh Lupoi said. “To be winning at half and come out the way we did is really disappointing.” When California beat SMU 38-35 in last year's regular-season finale, a loss that kept the Mustangs from making the Atlantic Coast Conference championship game for the second year in a row, Raphael scored a game-winning 2-yard TD run in the final minute for the Bears. “I just told him I’m glad he’s in the right jersey this time,” Lashlee said. Sagapolutele starting again for Bears Cal's left-handed quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele started for the first time in three games since a concussion late in the first half Oct. 3 at UNLV. He completed 27 of 37 passes for 265 yards and a touchdown. He threw for 330 yards and four TDs in last year's win over SMU. Sagapolutele missed the win over Virginia Tech two weeks ago, and Jackson Brousseau started again last week, though Sagapolutele threw a touchdown in the fourth quarter of the 41-7 home loss to Wake Forest. Finally some separation for the Mustangs After so many close games, the Mustangs in the second half had the kind of offensive outburst that they have been waiting for — 42 points and 306 of their 492 total yards after halftime. “That’s what we needed,” Lashlee said. “We felt like it was close, it was coming. It came at a good time for us.” SMU had scored a combined 48 points in its previous two games since pulling out a 34-24 win over second-year Bowl Subdivision team Missouri State. The takeaway California: The Bears have lost four of their last five games. SMU: The Mustangs, who scored TDs on seven consecutive drives overall, are 11-0 at home and 18-3 overall in ACC games since joining that league in 2024. ... SMU is 24-2 in its last 26 home games while averaging 44 points in those games. Up next California is at N.C. State for the second of three consecutive road games next Saturday. SMU plays its only road game in a seven-week stretch at Syracuse. The Mustangs also had five home games and an open date in that span. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full college football coverage here
